appIds.title: App IDs or Play Store URLs
appIds.description: Google Play package names (e.g. com.spotify.music) OR full Play Store URLs (e.g. https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.spotify.music&hl=en) — paste either, the package name is extracted from the URL's ?id= param.

searchTerms.title: Search terms
searchTerms.description: Alternative to App IDs: search terms; the top matching app(s) for each term will have their reviews fetched.

country.title: Country code
country.description: Play Store country code (affects app availability and review language).

language.title: Language code
language.description: Language for reviews and app details.

sort.title: Sort order
sort.description: Review sort order. Note: the fetch cap (maxReviewsPerApp) is applied to this sort order BEFORE ratingFilter, so RATING sort fills the cap with the highest-rated reviews first — hunting for low ratings with ratingFilter/maxScore returns 0 rows even when low-rated reviews exist, and raising maxReviewsPerApp does NOT help (verified 2026-09-25: on Spotify even the 5000 maximum kept 0 rows, all 5000 fetched were 5★). Use NEWEST (the default) when filtering for specific star ratings.

maxReviewsPerApp.title: Max reviews per app
maxReviewsPerApp.description: Fetch cap per app, counted before rating/keyword/appVersion/date filters are applied — a low cap combined with a narrow filter can miss matches deeper in the feed (see README FAQ). Raising it cannot help when sort=RATING excludes the star ratings you want; switch to NEWEST instead.

includeAppDetails.title: Include app details record
includeAppDetails.description: Also push one extra item per app with title, developer, rating, installs, price, description.

maxResults.title: Max total results
maxResults.description: Hard cap across all apps and app-detail records.

minScore.title: Minimum star rating
minScore.description: Only keep reviews with a star rating >= this (1-5).

maxScore.title: Maximum star rating
maxScore.description: Only keep reviews with a star rating <= this (1-5).

ratingFilter.title: Exact star ratings
ratingFilter.description: Only keep reviews whose star rating is one of these values, e.g. [1, 2, 5]. Use this instead of Minimum/Maximum when you want a non-contiguous set (Min/Max can only express a range). Applied on top of Min/Max if both are set.

keyword.title: Keyword filter
keyword.description: Only keep reviews whose title or text contains this word/phrase (case-insensitive). For several words, use "Keyword filters (any of)" below. Leading/trailing spaces are ignored. Accented letters are Unicode-normalized before matching, so "café" matches regardless of which Unicode form (composed or decomposed) you typed it in.

keywords.title: Keyword filters (any of)
keywords.description: Only keep reviews whose title or text contains AT LEAST ONE of these words/phrases (case-insensitive). Combined with the single Keyword filter using AND if both are set.

appVersions.title: App versions
appVersions.description: Only keep reviews written against one of these app versions, e.g. ["9.0.30.567"]. Note: Google Play leaves the version null on many reviews — those are dropped when this filter is set.

minThumbsUp.title: Minimum thumbs up
minThumbsUp.description: Only keep reviews with at least this many "helpful" votes (thumbs up) from other users. Google Play always reports this as 0 on a review with no votes, never null, so no reviews are dropped for missing data the way an app-version filter can drop null versions.

replyFilter.title: Developer reply
replyFilter.description: "Has a reply" finds reviews the developer already responded to (e.g. to audit response quality). "No reply" finds reviews still waiting for a response — the common support-queue use case.

minReviewLength.title: Minimum review text length
minReviewLength.description: Only keep reviews whose text is at least this many characters long. Filters out low-effort one-word/emoji-only reviews. A review with no text at all (title-only, or a bare star rating) is always dropped once this is set, since it can never meet a length floor above 0.

sinceDate.title: Since date
sinceDate.description: Only keep reviews posted on/after this date (ISO 8601, e.g. 2026-01-01).

untilDate.title: Until date
untilDate.description: Only keep reviews posted on/before this date (ISO 8601, e.g. 2026-06-01).

watchLabel.title: Watch label (only new reviews since last run)
watchLabel.description: Optional. Name a saved watch (e.g. "my-app-alerts") and this run returns ONLY reviews not delivered under that same label and filter set before, instead of the same top-of-feed reviews every time. The first run for a label is a free baseline: it records the reviews that already exist (walking at least 1000 per app, up to 5000 total) and returns zero rows. Run it again later — on a schedule, typically — to get only what is new. The baseline is kept in your own Apify account (a named key-value store "fetchsmith-google-play-reviews-watch"), keyed by label plus a fingerprint of apps/search terms/country/language/sort and every rating, keyword, app-version and date filter, so changing any of those starts a fresh baseline instead of hiding newly-matching reviews as "already seen". Use sort=NEWEST. App-detail records are only returned on a run where that app actually has a new review, so a run with nothing new costs nothing.

webhookUrl.title: Webhook URL (notify on completion)
webhookUrl.description: Optional. An http(s) URL to POST a small JSON summary to when the run finishes — reviews pushed, watch-label new count if Watch label is set, and the run's dataset ID so you can fetch the results. A convenience for callers who want a completion ping without setting up an Apify platform webhook (which needs separate Console/API configuration per Task, not per run). Best-effort: a failed or slow webhook is logged as a warning and never fails the run or affects charging — it fires after every review has already been pushed and charged. Leave empty to skip.
